indicators.name: Bribery depth (% of public transactions where a gift or informal payment was requested)
indicators.sourceNote: The depth of Bribery is the percentage of instances in which a firm was either expected or requested to provide a gift or informal payment during solicitations for public services, licenses or permits. This measure uses data from 6 survey questions for each firm. For purposes of computation, a refusal to answer a particular survey question is considered an affirmative answer.

indicators.name: Bribery incidence (percent of firms experiencing at least one bribe payment request)
indicators.sourceNote: The percent of firms experiencing at least one bribe payment request across 6 public transactions dealing with utilities access, permits, licenses, and taxes.

indicators.name: Percent of firms expected to give gifts in meetings with tax officials
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms expected to give gifts or informal payments during meetings with tax officials.

indicators.name: Percent of firms expected to give gifts to get an operating license
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms expected to give gifts or informal payments to get an operating license. Spontaneous refusals to the question are treated as a Yes.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying corruption as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying corruption as a "major" or "very severe" obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms expected to give gifts to secure government contract
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider that firms with characteristics similar to theirs are making informal payments or giving gifts to public officials to secure government contract.

indicators.name: Value of gift expected to secure a government contract (% of contract value)
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of contract value expected as a gift to secure government contract. Only firms that have confirmed that they have secured or attempted to secure a government contract in the last 12 months were required to answer this question.

indicators.name: Percent of firms expected to give gifts to public officials "to get things done"
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider that firms with characteristics similar to theirs are making informal payments or giving gifts to public officials to "get things done" with regard to customs, taxes, licenses, regulations, services etc.

indicators.name: Percent of firms expected to give gifts to get an electrical connection
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms expected to give gifts or informal payments to get an electrical connection.

indicators.name: Percent of firms expected to give gifts to get a water connection
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms expected to give gifts or informal payments to get a water connection.

indicators.name: Percent of firms expected to give gifts to get a construction permit
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms expected to give gifts or informal payments to get a construction permit.

indicators.name: Percent of firms expected to give gifts to get an import license
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms expected to give gifts or informal payments to get an import license.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying the courts system as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying functioning of the courts as major constraint. The computation of the indicator is based on the rating of the obstacle as a potential constraint to the current operations of the establishment.

indicators.name: Percent of firms paying for security
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms paying for security, for example equipment, personnel, or professional security services.

indicators.name: Percent of firms experiencing losses due to theft and vandalism
indicators.sourceNote: Percent of firms experiencing losses due to theft, robbery, vandalism or arson that occurred on the establishment's premises

indicators.name: If the establishment pays for security, average security costs (% of annual sales)
indicators.sourceNote: Average security costs as a percentage of total annual sales for firms that pay for security.

indicators.name: If there were losses, average losses due to theft and vandalism (% of annual sales)
indicators.sourceNote: If there were losses, estimated losses as a result of theft, robbery, vandalism or arson that occurred on establishment's premises calculated as a percentage of annual sales.

indicators.name: Products shipped to supply domestic markets that were lost due to theft (% of product value)
indicators.sourceNote: Value of losses of products, due to theft, while in transit to domestic markets.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying crime, theft and disorder as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying crime, theft and disorder as a "major" or "very severe" obstacle.

indicators.name: Annual employment growth (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Annualized growth of permanent full-time workers expressed as a percentage. Annual employment growth is the change in full-time employment reported in the current fiscal year from a previous period. For most countries the difference between the two fiscal year periods is two years. However, for some countries the interval is three years. Hence, an annualized measure is used.

indicators.name: Age of the establishment (years)
indicators.sourceNote: Age of the firm based on the year in which the firm began operations.

indicators.name: Proportion of private domestic ownership in a firm (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of the firm owned by domestic individuals, companies or organizations.

indicators.name: Percent of firms with at least 10% of foreign ownership
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that have at least 10% owned by private foreign individuals, companies or organizations.

indicators.name: Percent of firms with at least 10% of government/state ownership
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms where the government or state has at least a 10% share in ownership of the firm.

indicators.name: Percent of firms with legal status of Sole Proprietorship
indicators.sourceNote: Percent of firms with legal status of Sole Proprietorship

indicators.name: Percent of firms buying fixed assets
indicators.sourceNote: Percent of firms buying fixed assets such as machinery, equipment, land or buildings.

indicators.name: Proportion of investment financed internally (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Estimated proportion of purchases of fixed assets that was financed from internal funds/retained earnings.

indicators.name: Value of collateral needed for a loan (% of the loan amount)
indicators.sourceNote: Value of collateral needed for a loan or line of credit as a percentage of the loan value or the value of the line of credit.

indicators.name: Proportion of loans requiring collateral (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Loans requiring collateral in order to get the financing.

indicators.name: Percent of firms using banks to finance investments
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms using banks to finance purchases of fixed assets.

indicators.name: Percent of firms using banks to finance working capital
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms using bank loans to finance working capital.

indicators.name: Percent of firms with a bank loan/line of credit
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms with bank loans or line of credit.

indicators.name: Percent of firms with a checking or savings account
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms with a checking or savings account.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying access to finance as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying access/cost of finance as a "major" or "very severe" obstacle.

indicators.name: Proportion of investment financed by banks (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Estimated proportion of purchases of fixed assets that was financed from bank loans.

indicators.name: Percent of firms not needing a loan
indicators.sourceNote: Percent of firms that did not apply for a loan in the last fiscal year because they did not need a loan. The denominator is the number of firms who did and did not apply for a loan. The numerator is the number of firms who did not apply for a loan and also stated that they did not need a loan.

indicators.name: Percent of firms whose recent loan application was rejected
indicators.sourceNote: Percent of firms whose recent loan application was rejected.

indicators.name: Percent of firms using supplier/customer credit to finance working capital
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms using credit from suppliers and advances from customers to finance working capital.

indicators.name: Proportion of working capital financed by banks (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Proportion of the working capital that was financed by bank loans.

indicators.name: Percent of firms with female participation in ownership
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms with females among the owners.

indicators.name: Proportion of permanent full-time workers that are female (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of full-time workers that are female.

indicators.name: Proportion of permanent full-time non-production workers that are female (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of permanent full-time non-production workers that are female.

indicators.name: Percent of firms with a female top manager
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms with females as the top manager.

indicators.name: Proportion of permanent full-time production workers that are female (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of permanent full-time production workers that are female.

indicators.name: Percent of firms with majority female ownership
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms with majority female ownership

indicators.name: Percent of firms competing against unregistered or informal firms
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms competing against unregistered or informal firms.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying practices of competitors in the informal sector as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying practices of competitors in the informal sector as major constraint. The computation of the indicator is based on the rating of the obstacle as a potential constraint to the current operations of the establishment.

indicators.name: Percent of firms formally registered when they started operations in the country
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms formally registered when they started operations in the country.

indicators.name: Number of years firm operated without formal registration
indicators.sourceNote: Average number of years firms operated without formal registration. This indicator is computed only for the firms that did not have a formal registration when they started their operations in the country.

indicators.name: Days to obtain an electrical connection (upon application)
indicators.sourceNote: Average wait, in days, experienced to obtain electrical connection from the day this establishment applied for it to the day it received the service.

indicators.name: If a generator is used, average proportion of electricity from a generator (%)
indicators.sourceNote: If a generator is used, what percentage of electricity comes from a generator

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying transportation as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying transportation as a major constraint. The computation of the indicator is based on the rating of the obstacle as a potential constraint to the current operations of the establishment.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying electricity as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying electricity as a major constraint. The computation of the indicator is based on the rating of the obstacle as a potential constraint to the current operations of the establishment.

indicators.name: Proportion of products lost to breakage or spoilage during shipping to domestic markets (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of products shipped to supply domestic markets lost due to breakage or spoilage.

indicators.name: Percent of firms experiencing electrical outages
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that experienced power outages over the last complete fiscal year.

indicators.name: Percent of firms experiencing water insufficiencies
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that experienced insufficient water supply for production over the last complete fiscal year.

indicators.name: Number of electrical outages in a typical month
indicators.sourceNote: Average number of power outages in a typical month.

indicators.name: If there were outages, average duration of a typical electrical outage (hours)
indicators.sourceNote: Average duration of power outages (hours) conditional on having a power outage.

indicators.name: If there were outages, average losses due to electrical outages (% of annual sales)
indicators.sourceNote: If there were outages, average losses due to electrical outages, as percentage of total annual sales.

indicators.name: Number of water insufficiencies in a typical month
indicators.sourceNote: Average number of water shortages in a typical month in the last fiscal year.

indicators.name: Percent of firms owning or sharing a generator
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms owning or sharing a generator.

indicators.name: Percent of firms with an internationally-recognized quality certification
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that have an internationally-recognized quality certification, i.e. ISO 9000, 9002 or 14000.

indicators.name: Percent of firms that spend on R&D
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that spent on formal research and development activities during the last fiscal year.

indicators.name: Percent of firms with an annual financial statement reviewed by external auditors
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms with their annual financial statement reviewed by an external auditor.

indicators.name: Capacity utilization (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Capacity utilization based on comparison of the current output with the maximum output possible using the current inputs.

indicators.name: Percent of firms using technology licensed from foreign companies
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms using technology licensed from foreign companies.

indicators.name: Percent of firms having their own Web site
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms using website for business related activities, i.e. sales, product promotion etc.

indicators.name: Percent of firms using e-mail to interact with clients/suppliers
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms using email to interact with clients or suppliers.

indicators.name: Percent of firms that introduced a new product/service
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that introduced new or significantly improved products or services over the last three years.

indicators.name: Percent of firms whose new product/service is also new to the main market
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that introduced new or significantly improved products or services over the last three years that were also new for the firms' main market.

indicators.name: Percent of firms that introduced a process innovation
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that introduced any new or significantly improved process.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing access to finance as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider access to finance to be the Biggest Obstacle

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing labor regulations as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider labor regulations to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing political instability as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider political instability to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing practices of the informal sector as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider practices of competitors in the informal sector to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing tax administration as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider the tax administration to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing tax rates as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider tax rates to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing transportation as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider transport to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing access to land as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider access to land to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing business licensing and permits as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider business licensing and permits to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing corruption as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider corruption to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing courts as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider courts to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing crime, theft and disorder as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider crime, theft and disorder to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing customs and trade regulations as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider customs and trade regulations to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing electricity as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider electricity to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms choosing inadequately educated workforce as their biggest obstacle
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of establishments that consider an inadequately educated workforce to be the Biggest Obstacle.

indicators.name: Real annual labor productivity growth (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Annual labor productivity growth is measured by a percentage change in labor productivity between the last completed fiscal year and a previous period, where labor productivity is sales divided by the number of full- time permanent workers. All sales values are deflated to 2009 using each country's GDP deflators.

indicators.name: Days to obtain an import license
indicators.sourceNote: Average wait, in days, to obtain import license.

indicators.name: Days to obtain an operating license
indicators.sourceNote: The average wait, in days, to obtain an operating license.

indicators.name: Days to obtain a construction-related permit
indicators.sourceNote: Average wait, in days, to obtain construction-related permit.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying business licensing and permits as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying business licensing and permits as "major" or "very severe" obstacle.

indicators.name: Senior management time spent dealing with the requirements of government regulation (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Average percentage of senior management's time that is spent in a typical week dealing with requirements imposed by government regulations (eg. taxes, customs, labor regulations, licensing and registration), including dealings with officials, completing forms, et cetera.

indicators.name: If there were visits, average number of visits or required meetings with tax officials
indicators.sourceNote: If there were a positive number of visits or required meeting with tax officials, what was the average number?

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying tax rates as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying tax rates as a "major" or "very severe" obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying tax administration as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying tax administration as a "major" or "very severe" obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms visited or required to meet with tax officials
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that were visited or inspected by tax officials or were required to meet with them over the last year.

indicators.name: Real annual sales growth (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Real annual sales growth is measured as a percentage change in sales between the last completed fiscal year and a previous period. All sales values are deflated to 2009 using each country's GDP deflators.

indicators.name: Days to clear direct exports through customs
indicators.sourceNote: Average number of days to clear direct exports through customs.

indicators.name: Percent of firms using material inputs and/or supplies of foreign origin
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that use material inputs and/or supplies of foreign origin.

indicators.name: Percent of firms exporting directly (at least 10% of sales)
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that export directly at least 10% of their total annual sales.

indicators.name: Percent of firms exporting directly or indirectly (at least 10% of sales)
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms that export directly or indirectly at least 10% of their total annual sales.

indicators.name: Days to clear imports from customs
indicators.sourceNote: Average number of days to clear imports from customs.

indicators.name: Proportion of total sales that are exported directly (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Sales exported directly as percentage of total sales.

indicators.name: Proportion of total inputs that are of foreign origin (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of material inputs and/or supplies of foreign origin.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying customs and trade regulations as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying customs and trade regulations as a "major" or "very severe" obstacle.

indicators.name: Percent of firms offering formal training
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms offering formal training programs for its permanent, full-time employees.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying an inadequately educated workforce as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying labor skill level as a major constraint. The computation of the indicator is based on the rating of the obstacle as a potential constraint to the current operations of the establishment.

indicators.name: Number of workers
indicators.sourceNote: Number of workers, including permanent and temporary workers. The number of temporary workers is adjusted for the number of months of their employment.

indicators.name: Proportion of production workers (out of all permanent workers)
indicators.sourceNote: Proportion of production workers out of all permanent workers*.

indicators.name: Proportion of temporary workers (out of all workers)
indicators.sourceNote: The proportion of temporary workers out of all workers.

indicators.name: Proportion of permanent workers (out of all workers)
indicators.sourceNote: The proportion of permanent workers out of all workers.

indicators.name: Proportion of skilled workers (out of all production workers) (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Proportion of skilled workers out of all production workers*.

indicators.name: Proportion of workers offered formal training (%)
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of permanent, full-time employees that have received formal training.

indicators.name: Years of the top manager's experience working in the firm's sector
indicators.sourceNote: Years of experience of the top manager working in the sector.

indicators.name: Percent of firms identifying labor regulations as a major constraint
indicators.sourceNote: Percentage of firms identifying labor regulations as a "major" or "very severe" obstacle.
